title: fdtdKit: taking openEMS towards the memory ceiling of an Apple M5
description:
fdtdKit makes the open-source EC-FDTD field solver openEMS faster on Apple Silicon. The repository holds the changes as patches (39 for openEMS, 1 for CSXCAD), the benchmark harness, every measured table, the paper with its sources, and the command line emskit fdtd that runs the checks and benchmarks.

On an Apple M5 the multithreaded CPU engine runs 1.95 to 6.89 times as fast as openEMS v0.37.0 on six models of 0.1 to 7.9 million cells, with bit-identical port signals, S-parameters and far-field dumps. A GPU engine with diamond-shaped temporal blocks (Metal) is up to 1.47 times as fast again on large models.

The code, the measurements and most of the text were produced with AI assistants (Claude, Anthropic), directed by the author; the paper's Disclosure section gives the details.
notes: The harness, scripts, results and the Swift package are under GPL-3.0-or-later; the paper (paper/) is under CC BY 4.0; the CSXCAD patch is under LGPL-3.0-or-later like CSXCAD itself.
